planting.note: Set container plants out in spring to early summer in well-drained soil; full sun keeps the chartreuse foliage from fading toward plain green.

directions: Snippet Lime is grown chiefly for its glowing chartreuse foliage rather than flower power, though it does carry a modest flush of pink trumpet blooms through late spring and summer without deadheading. Plant in full sun, since shade dulls the leaf color toward ordinary green, in well-drained soil; its tight, rounded, knee-high habit suits foundation beds and mixed containers where a full-size weigela would overwhelm the space. It was patented (US Plant Patent PP30,264) under the breeding code 'VUKOZ047213' as a foliage-focused companion to the darker-leaved Snippet Dark Pink release in the same dwarf series. Shape lightly right after the main spring flush rather than shearing hard, since next year's wood sets soon after bloom.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil; shear off the first flush of spent flowers to push a second round of bloom.

directions: Double Play Pink stands out among its Proven Winners series-mates for flower color saturation, opening noticeably deeper, truer pink clusters than the other Double Play introductions, above new growth that emerges dark burgundy-red before settling to green for summer. Grow it in average, well-drained soil in full sun for the richest bloom color and tightest mounded form, and shear the spent flower heads after the first flush to encourage reliable summer rebloom. It carries US Plant Patent PP26,995 under the breeding code 'SMNSJMFP' and, like the rest of the series, tolerates heat and average garden soil with minimal care once established. An occasional renewal cut to the oldest stems in late winter keeps the mound dense rather than twiggy.

planting.note: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part sun; the brightest chartreuse foliage color develops with the most direct light.

directions: Glow Girl Pink pairs the native birchleaf spirea's tough, disease-resistant constitution with bright chartreuse foliage held all season and clusters of pink flowers in late spring, a color combination the original white-flowered Glow Girl birchleaf spirea lacks. Grow in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part sun, since fuller light sustains both the strongest foliage color and the heaviest bloom on its loose, compact mound. Patented in the US as PP37,503 under the code 'SMNSBDOU', it was bred as a pink-flowered companion to the earlier white-flowered Glow Girl selection. It needs only an occasional light shearing after bloom to keep the habit neat, and is otherwise low-maintenance once established.
